Welcome toDesperate Housewives

Behind every perfect house is a secret.

“Welcome to Wisteria Lane, where the lawns are perfect, the smiles are convincing, and nobody is telling the whole truth.”

An 80–90 minute evening · B1–C1 English
Chapter I · 15 minutes

The Perfect Neighbourhood, the Perfect Lies

PollWhole groupThink · Pair · ShareVocabulary
debtlonelinessan affair? exhaustionresentmentanxietya lie
The main question

Why do people try so hard to make their lives look perfect?

Stage A

First impressions

Poll · 3 min

“Which of these do people most often pretend to have under control?”

Tap an option once for each vote. Then ask a few people to briefly explain their choice.

Stage B

Behind the perfect image

Whole group · 5 min
  1. Is pretending to be happy sometimes a way of protecting yourself?Follow-up: Can you think of a real-life example, without naming anyone?
  2. Is there a difference between keeping your private life private and deliberately misleading people?Follow-up: Where exactly is the line? Give an example of each.
  3. Do people actually want a perfect life, or do they want other people to believe they have one?Follow-up: What might someone gain or lose by being honest?
Need a little help expressing yourself?
  • I think people feel pressured to … because …
  • One reason people hide their problems is …
  • There's a difference between privacy and dishonesty because …
  • People may be afraid of being judged for …
  • In some cases, pretending to be happy can …
Stage C

Mary Alice's secret

Think · Pair · Share · 5 min
From the series · Season 1, Episodes 1 & 4

Mary Alice Young seemed to have the perfect suburban life: a lovely home, a devoted husband, Paul, and a teenage son. After her sudden death in the very first episode, her closest friends — Susan, Lynette, Bree and Gabrielle — sort through her belongings and find an anonymous blackmail note addressed to her. Someone knew her secret and was threatening to reveal it. The friends have to decide what to do, and a few episodes later they show the note to Paul.

1 Think alone · 30 sec2 Discuss in pairs · 2 min3 Share with the group · 2 min
  1. Were the friends right to show Paul the note, or should they have let Mary Alice keep her secret?
  2. Does a person's right to privacy end when they die — or when their secret could hurt other people?

“On Wisteria Lane, appearances can be misleading. But the most interesting secrets often emerge inside the home — especially in relationships.”

Chapter II · Couple One · 12 minutes

Love, Power, Money & Control

Gabrielle and Carlos Solis

Case fileWhole groupReal dilemmaVocabulary
Case File No. 01
Relationship overview

From the outside, they have everything: a beautiful house, expensive things and a lot of passion. Underneath, the relationship is constantly negotiated — through money, status, jealousy and the question of who really holds the power.

Subject A

Gabrielle Solis

A former model who enjoys glamour and status. Quick-witted, fiercely independent and often bored by the life she was promised.

Subject B

Carlos Solis

An ambitious, successful businessman who provides the luxury lifestyle — and tends to expect loyalty and control in return.

PassionAmbitionMoneyStatusJealousyTrustPower
Discuss

Three questions

Whole group · 4 min
  1. Can two people genuinely love each other and still have an unhealthy relationship?
  2. How can money and financial dependence affect the balance of power between partners?
  3. Is jealousy a sign of love, insecurity, or a desire for control?
Need a little help expressing yourself?
  • Their biggest problem seems to be …
  • I think this conflict stems from …
  • Both partners have a point because …
  • The way they handle conflict suggests that …
  • A healthier way to approach this situation would be …
The dilemma

The affair

Pairs → group · 4 min
From the series · Seasons 1–2

Gabrielle has the luxury lifestyle she always wanted, but Carlos neglects her and talks down to her. Lonely and bored, she begins a secret affair with John, their young gardener. Later, when Carlos is in jail over his business dealings, he learns about the affair and refuses to forgive her.

  1. Does Carlos's behaviour explain Gabrielle's affair, or is she fully responsible for her own choice?
  2. Can a marriage built on money and status survive this kind of betrayal?
  3. If you were Gabrielle's friend, what would you have told her before the affair began?
Final evaluation

Would you describe this relationship as passionate, toxic, complicated, or some combination of the three?

Chapter III · Couple Two · 12 minutes

Marriage, Mental Load & the Battle for Control

Lynette and Tom Scavo

Case fileWhole groupPairsReal dilemmaVocabulary
Case File No. 02
Relationship overview

A loving, loud, exhausted partnership. Their conflicts rarely start with grand betrayals — they start with childcare, chores, schedules and careers, and grow into a constant negotiation over who sacrifices what.

Subject A

Lynette Scavo

A former high-flying advertising executive who left her career to raise their children. Organised, competitive and used to being in charge.

Subject B

Tom Scavo

A warm, easy-going husband and father whose own ambitions and changing plans often collide with Lynette's.

ParentingHouseholdCareerExhaustionCompromisePower struggles
Discuss

Three questions

Whole group · 4 min
  1. Why do small everyday disagreements sometimes become major relationship conflicts?
  2. Is an equal relationship always a 50/50 relationship?
  3. Is compromise always healthy, or can it turn into resentment?
Need a little help expressing yourself?
  • Their biggest problem seems to be …
  • I think this conflict stems from …
  • Both partners have a point because …
  • In a fair relationship, both partners should … otherwise …
  • A healthier way to approach this situation would be …
Pair activity · 3 min

Divide the load

You are an imaginary couple, Partner A and Partner B. Tap each task to assign it: A, B, Shared or Outsource. Then discuss: is your split fair? Is fair the same as 50/50?

The dilemma

The pizzeria

Pairs → group · 3 min
From the series · Season 3

Tom tells Lynette he wants to open a pizzeria. Lynette is shocked: with a big family to support, she sees a serious financial risk. Then she discovers that Tom has already signed a lease without consulting her. Later, Lynette quits her own job to work with him at the restaurant — and the two of them keep clashing over who makes the decisions.

  1. Was Tom wrong to sign the lease without Lynette, or was it the only way he could make the pizzeria happen?
  2. Should one partner be able to stop the other from taking a big career risk?
  3. When Lynette joins the business, is she supporting Tom or taking control?
Final evaluation

Can two people be right about their own needs and still be unfair to each other?

Chapter IV · Couple Three · 12 minutes

Vulnerability, Trust & Emotional Honesty

Susan Mayer and Mike Delfino

Case fileWhole groupPairsReal dilemmaVocabulary
Case File No. 03
Relationship overview

An affectionate, romantic and often chaotic pairing. The love seems obvious to everyone — the difficulty is saying what they really feel, trusting what they don't know, and not expecting the other person to guess.

Subject A

Susan Mayer

A divorced children's book illustrator and single mother. Romantic, warm, impulsive and famously clumsy.

Subject B

Mike Delfino

The handsome plumber who moves onto the street — quiet, protective and carrying a past he doesn't easily talk about.

AffectionVulnerabilityMiscommunicationTrustExpectationsHonesty
Discuss

Three questions

Whole group · 4 min
  1. Why do people sometimes hide their true feelings from someone they love?
  2. Is honesty always the best policy in a relationship?
  3. Should your partner be responsible for making you feel secure?
Need a little help expressing yourself?
  • I get the impression that … is afraid of …
  • I think this conflict stems from …
  • Instead of saying what they need, they …
  • The way they handle conflict suggests that …
  • A healthier way to approach this situation would be …
Pair activity · 3 min

Say it directly

Each card shows an indirect message. In pairs, rewrite it as an honest, direct message — then tap the card to compare with one possible version.

The dilemma

The search

Pairs → group · 3 min
From the series · Season 1

Susan has fallen for her mysterious new neighbour, the plumber Mike Delfino, but he is very private about his past. Suspicious, she searches his house and finds a gun and a large amount of cash. When Mike realises she has been going through his things, he breaks up with her. Later in the season, Susan discovers that Mike has a criminal record.

  1. Was Susan wrong to search Mike's house, or did his secrecy give her a good reason?
  2. How much of your past do you owe a new partner — and when should you tell them?
  3. Who broke the trust first: Mike by hiding things, or Susan by snooping?
Final evaluation

Is a healthy relationship about finding someone who understands you naturally, or learning how to explain yourself?

Chapter V · 8 minutes

Same Problem. Three Different Reactions.

Small groupsWhole-group comparison
The shared situation

“One partner discovers that the other has made a major decision without discussing it first. The decision affects both of their lives, but the person who made it believes they had a good reason.”

How would Gabrielle & Carlos, Lynette & Tom and Susan & Mike each react? Base your predictions on the dynamics you've discussed tonight.

The board

Interactive comparison

Groups · 4 min

These are interpretations and predictions, not facts from the series. There are no right answers — only well-argued ones.

Compare

Follow-up questions

Whole group · 3 min
  1. Which couple seems most likely to forgive the other person — and what makes you think so?
  2. Which relationship dynamic seems most familiar to real life?
Need a little help comparing?
  • Unlike …, … would probably …
  • Both couples would …, but the difference is that …
  • I'd expect … to react more … than …
  • It's a generalisation, but I think …
  • I might be wrong, but my prediction is based on …
Chapter VI · 15 minutes

Can You Be a Good Person and Still Do Bad Things?

On Wisteria Lane, almost nobody is completely innocent or completely guilty. People act out of fear, love, jealousy, ambition, insecurity — or the desire to protect themselves. Tonight, you decide what that means.

Can you be a good person and still do bad things?

Stage A

Moral dilemmas

Whole group · 4 min
  1. If someone lies because they are afraid of losing the person they love, are they selfish or vulnerable?
  2. Should we judge people by the harm they cause or by the reasons behind their actions?
  3. Does suffering explain harmful behaviour, or does it become an excuse?
Need a little help expressing yourself?
  • I believe a person's intentions matter because …
  • I don't think good intentions excuse …
  • We should distinguish between … and …
  • Someone can take responsibility for their actions by …
  • Whether forgiveness is deserved depends on …
Stage B

One big question

Whole group · 3 min

“Are people more than the worst thing they have ever done?”

Stage C

Bree's cover-up

Pairs → group · 5 min
From the series · Season 1, Episodes 7–8

Bree's teenage son, Andrew, drives drunk and runs over Juanita Solis — Carlos's mother. When Bree and her husband Rex find out what Andrew has done, they decide to cover it up to protect their son instead of going to the police, while the Solis family has no idea who hurt her.

  1. Is Bree a loving mother or a bad person here — or can she be both?
  2. What would genuine accountability have looked like for Andrew?
  3. Should loyalty to your family ever come before doing what is right?
  4. What would you need to see before believing that Andrew had changed?
Round the room · one or two sentences each

Can you be a good person and still do bad things?

Refer to a character, a dilemma or an idea from tonight. The aim is not agreement — it's reflection.

Epilogue · 5 minutes

Behind every perfect house is a story.

i.

What idea from tonight's discussion challenged your perspective?

ii.

Which character did you understand differently after this discussion?

iii.

What question are you still thinking about?

“Thank you for joining us on Wisteria Lane. Remember: things are rarely as simple as they seem.”
